title: UAT quiz: Hazira gas release and fire, 2020
status: Learning purposes: not a statutory document

bottom_line.text: A repaired joint is proved only by a recorded test at design pressure.

items.question: A gasket on a high-pressure meter has been replaced. What proves the joint before return to service?

options.text: A recorded test at design pressure, with a witness
Bringing the line up to operating pressure
A visual check that the bolts are tight

items.why: Knowing which test proves a repaired joint.
items.answer: A recorded test at design pressure, with a witness; operating pressure does not prove it.
items.good_evidence: The learner names the test pressure and where the record is kept.

items.question: Which of these are warning signs before a return to service?

options.text: A seal or gasket that is not the original part
No test record at design pressure
A permit signed by the issuer

items.why: Recognising the conditions that should stop a return to service.
items.answer: A part that is not the original, and no test record at design pressure.
items.good_evidence: Both warning signs named without prompting.

items.question: The gas detectors at the terminal shut the plant down automatically.
items.why: Knowing what the gas alarm did and did not do.
items.answer: False: the detectors showed an alarm on a panel only, with no automatic shutdown.
items.good_evidence: The learner says who must act when an alarm only displays.

items.question: In two words: at what pressure must a repaired high-pressure joint be tested?
items.good_evidence: The learner gives the words without a prompt.

items.question: On your unit, who can stop a return to service when the test record is missing?
items.why: Knowing who holds the stop in practice.
items.answer: Anyone on the job can ask for the record, and the supervisor holds the return to service until it is there.
items.good_evidence: The learner names a role and the place the record is kept.
